close_reason: Fixed in commit d0a0bd4. metadata_query's doc-comment now includes runnable filter examples (typed condition shape and FilterOperator OR algebra shape) and a sort example (comparator-array with explicit isAscending). All examples are tagged ```ignore so they do not run as doctests but render in cargo doc output.
description:
src/methods/metadata.rs:158-199 — metadata_query's doc-comment names the canonical filter type:

    The filter value is typed by the caller; the canonical type is
    jmap_metadata_types::MetadataFilterCondition (§3.4.1) wrapped in
    jmap_types::query::Filter. This builder accepts a serde_json::Value
    so callers can mix filter conditions with FilterOperator algebra
    without forcing a single type through the API.

…and names the valid sort properties:

    Sort comparators MUST set property to one of id, @type,
    relatedType, relatedId, or isPrivate per §3.4.2; id MUST be
    supported by every server, the others SHOULD be supported.

But provides no construction example. A caller cannot tell from the doc:
- How to wrap a MetadataFilterCondition in a Filter<T> for the serde_json::Value parameter.
- How to construct a valid sort comparator (the JSON shape is { property: String, isAscending?: bool, collation?: String } per RFC 8620 §5.5 — not stated here, just spec-cross-referenced).
- Whether to pass jmap_types::query::Comparator or build the shape by hand.

A no_run doc-example showing:

    let filter = serde_json::to_value(MetadataFilterCondition::RelatedType(\"Email\".into()))?;
    let sort = json!([{ \"property\": \"id\", \"isAscending\": true }]);
    let resp = sc.metadata_query(Some(filter), Some(sort), None, Some(50)).await?;

…would close the contract gap. Underspecified per /review-library-supplement §underspecified.

Workspace-wide: same gap on email_query, mailbox_query, thread_query in mail-client. Propagate.
title: metadata_query: filter/sort doc-comments give type names but no construction example
